subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — All Tenses and Special Forms (W10)

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'The teacher teaches the students every day.'

options.option_text: The students were taught by the teacher every day.
The students are taught by the teacher every day.
The students will be taught by the teacher every day.
The students have been taught by the teacher every day.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Simple Present Active → Simple Present Passive: 'am/is/are + past participle.' The object 'students' becomes the subject; 'teacher' follows 'by.' Trap: 'were taught' is Simple Past Passive; 'will be taught' is Future Passive; 'have been taught' is Present Perfect Passive — all wrong tense for Simple Present.

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'She wrote a letter to her friend.'

options.option_text: A letter is written by her to her friend.
A letter has been written by her to her friend.
A letter was written by her to her friend.
A letter had been written by her to her friend.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Simple Past Active → Simple Past Passive: 'was/were + past participle.' 'Wrote' → 'was written.' Trap: 'is written' is Simple Present Passive; 'has been written' is Present Perfect Passive; 'had been written' is Past Perfect Passive — each shifts the tense incorrectly.

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'They are building a new stadium in the city.'

options.option_text: A new stadium was being built by them in the city.
A new stadium is being built by them in the city.
A new stadium has been built by them in the city.
A new stadium will be built by them in the city.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Present Continuous Active → Present Continuous Passive: 'is/are being + past participle.' 'Are building' → 'is being built.' The object 'stadium' (singular) takes 'is.' Trap: 'was being built' is Past Continuous Passive; 'has been built' is Present Perfect Passive — the ongoing action of the continuous tense must be preserved.

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'The police have arrested the thief.'

options.option_text: The thief was arrested by the police.
The thief is arrested by the police.
The thief has been arrested by the police.
The thief had been arrested by the police.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Present Perfect Active → Present Perfect Passive: 'has/have been + past participle.' 'Have arrested' → 'has been arrested' (object 'thief' is singular). Trap: 'was arrested' is Simple Past Passive; 'had been arrested' is Past Perfect Passive — both shift the time reference incorrectly.

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice (select the most natural form):
'Someone stole my wallet last night.'

options.option_text: My wallet was stolen by someone last night.
My wallet has been stolen last night.
My wallet was stolen last night.
My wallet is stolen last night.

questions.explanation: C is correct. When the agent is an indefinite pronoun like 'someone', it is typically omitted in the passive voice since it adds no information. 'Someone stole' → 'was stolen.' 'Last night' (time marker) stays. Trap: Option A retains 'by someone' — grammatically correct but unnatural and redundant; Option B uses wrong tense (Present Perfect); Option D uses wrong tense (Simple Present).

questions.stem:
Change to Active Voice:
'The match was won by India.'

options.option_text: India wins the match.
India had won the match.
India won the match.
India has won the match.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Simple Past Passive ('was won by') → Simple Past Active ('won'). The agent 'India' (after 'by') becomes the active subject. Trap: 'wins' is Simple Present; 'had won' is Past Perfect; 'has won' is Present Perfect — each deviates from the Simple Past tense of the original.

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'The manager had warned all employees before the inspection.'

options.option_text: All employees were warned by the manager before the inspection.
All employees have been warned by the manager before the inspection.
All employees had been warned by the manager before the inspection.
All employees would have been warned by the manager before the inspection.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Past Perfect Active → Past Perfect Passive: 'had been + past participle.' 'Had warned' → 'had been warned.' The Past Perfect is used to describe an action completed before another past action — this time reference must be preserved. Trap: 'were warned' is Simple Past Passive (drops the 'had'); 'would have been warned' is Conditional Perfect (wrong mood).

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'Will the government announce new economic policies?'

options.option_text: Are new economic policies announced by the government?
Will new economic policies be announced by the government?
Were new economic policies announced by the government?
Have new economic policies been announced by the government?

questions.explanation: B is correct. Simple Future Interrogative Active → Simple Future Interrogative Passive: 'Will + object + be + past participle + by + agent?' The interrogative word order places 'Will' at the start; 'announce' → 'be announced.' Trap: A uses Simple Present; C uses Simple Past; D uses Present Perfect — all wrong tenses for a future question.

questions.stem:
Change to Passive Voice:
'Nobody can deny the importance of education.'

options.option_text: The importance of education can be denied by nobody.
The importance of education cannot be denied by anyone.
The importance of education cannot be denied.
The importance of education was not denied.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Modal Active with indefinite negative subject → Modal Passive: 'nobody + can' becomes 'cannot.' The agent ('by nobody'/'by anyone') is omitted in the cleaner passive form. Rule: when active subject is 'nobody/no one', the passive uses 'cannot be + past participle' without restating the agent. Trap: A restates 'by nobody' (grammatically acceptable but awkward); B changes nobody→anyone (subtle but acceptable alternative — SSC prefers C); D incorrectly shifts from modal to Simple Past.

questions.stem:
Change to Active Voice:
'Let the work be done immediately.'

options.option_text: The work is done immediately.
The work must be done immediately.
Do the work immediately.
You should do the work immediately.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Passive Imperative ('Let + object + be + past participle') → Active Imperative (direct command). The subject 'you' is implied but not stated in an imperative. 'Let the work be done immediately' → 'Do the work immediately.' Trap: Option B adds 'must' (modal, not imperative); Option D adds 'you should' (advisory, not imperative); Option A converts to Simple Present (loses the command).
